title: Color psychology: Effects of perceiving color on psychological functioning in humans
authority: Elliot is the leading experimental color-psychology researcher (Color-in-Context Theory); the Annual Review is a peer-reviewed state-of-the-field venue.
caveats: Written by authors of the key studies, so it is partly self-reviewing. Explicitly says the field is young and that boundary conditions and real-world generalizability need work before applied recommendations. Several headline effects reviewed (red and performance, red and attraction) have had failed replications.

title: Color and psychological functioning: The effect of red on performance attainment
authority: Peer-reviewed series of experiments in a top general psychology journal; the founding study of the red-impairs-performance literature.
caveats: Small samples by modern standards (roughly 24-70 per experiment from memory). Later direct replications by Steele and others failed; a 2020 meta-analysis reports a small negative effect of red but with likely bias. Treat as a hypothesis, not a design rule. Bibliographic details from memory, not web-confirmed this session (search budget exhausted).

title: Failure to replicate the Mehta and Zhu (2009) color-priming effect on anagram solution times
authority: Peer-reviewed replication report by a psychologist at Appalachian State University; the standard citation for the failure of the blue/red cognitive-mode effect.
caveats: Tests one effect (Mehta & Zhu 2009), not red-and-performance generally. Volume, issue and pages not confirmed this session and left blank; DOI is taken from the confirmed Springer URL.

title: An ecological valence theory of human color preference
container: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
authority: Palmer is a leading perception scientist at UC Berkeley; peer-reviewed in PNAS with quantitative model comparison.
caveats: Correlational (r about .8 reported at the level of average ratings from US and Berkeley students); causal direction (do associations cause preference?) is argued, not proven. Samples were mostly young, US-based. Later work (Schloss, Lai et al.) refines it.

title: Universal patterns in color-emotion associations are further shaped by linguistic and geographic proximity
authority: Large cross-cultural study (4,598 participants, 30 nations, 22 languages) in a top psychology journal.
caveats: Measures stated associations with color words, not behavior or emotion induced by seeing color. Mostly university-student samples. Author list shortened here (the paper has many co-authors); complete from the DOI before print.

title: Color psychology: A critical review
container: Genetic, Social, and General Psychology Monographs
authority: A monograph-length critical review of the pre-1990 color psychology literature by experimental psychologists; the canonical skeptical review.
caveats: Dated; predates most modern work. Page range from memory. Its methodological critiques (uncontrolled lightness/saturation, tiny samples, no replication) still apply.

title: Effects of color on emotions
authority: Peer-reviewed, controlled study of Munsell-specified colors on the pleasure-arousal-dominance (PAD) scales; the best-known evidence that brightness and saturation, not hue, drive emotion ratings.
caveats: Ratings of small color patches by American undergraduates; not about interface contexts. Findings on hue effects are weak and not consistently replicated.

title: Exciting red and competent blue: The importance of color in marketing
container: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science
authority: Peer-reviewed marketing study linking logo colors to Aaker brand-personality dimensions.
caveats: Student/online samples, ratings of fictitious brands; effects are modest and context dependent. Not evidence for learning outcomes.

title: Waiting for the web: How screen color affects time perception
authority: Peer-reviewed marketing-psychology study on screen background color and perceived download time.
caveats: Small lab studies; no known strong replication. DOI and page range not confirmed, left blank. A figure of 53% faster perceived download circulates in blogs; not traced to the paper.

title: Guidelines for the use of color in ATC displays
publisher: Federal Aviation Administration, Office of Aviation Research (DOT/FAA/AR-99/52)
authority: US Department of Transportation human-factors report that synthesizes research into guidelines for color on safety-critical displays.
caveats: Written for air traffic control displays, not cockpits or learning apps; I could not read the full text, so specifics below are from the standard color-coding literature it summarizes and are marked approximate. FAA-HF-STD-010A (2020) now supersedes for ATC.

title: Color Universal Design (CUD): How to make figures and presentations that are friendly to colorblind people
authority: Authored by a Univ. of Tokyo medical-genetics researcher and designer working with color-blind scientists; source of the widely used 8-color CUD palette.
caveats: Not peer reviewed; a practical guide. Palette recommendations were checked by simulation and by color-blind participants but not formal trials.

title: A physiologically-based model for simulation of color vision deficiency
container: IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics
authority: Peer-reviewed; the model behind most CVD simulators in browsers and design tools.
caveats: A simulation approximates the average case; severity varies and simulators do not show individual experience. Validated with a small user study.

title: Points of view: Color blindness
authority: Wong (Broad Institute) wrote the Nature Methods Points of View series on visual communication for scientists.
caveats: One-page column; practical guidance, not an experiment. Full text is paywalled; details below come from excerpts and memory.

title: Psychophysics of reading. V. The role of contrast in normal vision
authority: Legge's lab at Minnesota is the central source for quantitative reading and contrast research; peer-reviewed psychophysics.
caveats: Small number of young normally sighted readers; rapid-serial-style drifting text; measures reading speed, not comprehension or comfort over long sessions.

title: Positive display polarity is advantageous for both younger and older adults
authority: Peer-reviewed human-factors experiments from Düsseldorf; the main empirical basis for 'dark text on light is better for reading'.
caveats: Online first 2013 (DOI confirmed by search); print volume, issue and pages not confirmed. A 2014 follow-up in Ergonomics by the same group argues the advantage is due to display luminance. Tests used acuity and proofreading in normal room light; not long reading sessions in dark rooms.

title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
authority: The international standard for web accessibility, including contrast success criteria 1.4.1, 1.4.3, 1.4.6, 1.4.11.
caveats: The WCAG 2 luminance contrast ratio is known to overstate contrast for some dark-mode pairs and to understate it for some mid-tones; APCA (Somers) is a proposed alternative for WCAG 3 draft but not a standard.

title: Dark mode: How users think about it and issues to avoid
authority: Nielsen Norman Group is a long-established usability research consultancy; the piece summarizes user research and literature on dark mode. Author attribution from memory, URL confirmed.
caveats: Practitioner synthesis, not peer reviewed. The individual author of the article could not be confirmed this session, so it is credited to the organization. URL confirmed by search.

title: Blue or red? Exploring the effect of color on cognitive task performances
authority: Published in Science; the most widely cited claim that red favors detail-oriented tasks and blue favors creative tasks.
caveats: Failed direct replication (Steele 2014) and other null results. Bibliographic details from memory; web confirmation was blocked when the search budget ran out. Treat the effect as unreliable.

title: Psychophysics of reading. XI. Comparing color contrast and luminance contrast
container: Journal of the Optical Society of America A
authority: Same Minnesota lab; direct test of whether chromatic contrast can substitute for luminance contrast in reading. A search result listed a file named for this paper at the lab site, which confirms it exists; volume, pages and DOI are from memory.
caveats: Small lab samples of young readers. Confirm volume, pages and DOI before print.

title: Computerized simulation of color appearance for dichromats
container: Journal of the Optical Society of America A
authority: Peer-reviewed vision-science paper by Mollon, a leading color-vision researcher; the basis of most dichromacy simulators.
caveats: Bibliographic details from memory, not web-confirmed (search budget exhausted). Based on reports of unilateral dichromats; simulation shows the average case.

title: Managing images in different cultures: A cross-national study of color meanings and preferences
authority: Peer-reviewed cross-national study of color meaning and preference in eight countries; widely cited in international marketing. Note: the second author's name is Hewett (the brief wrote Hewitt).
caveats: Bibliographic details from memory, not web-confirmed. Student samples, color-word and color-chip ratings; dated. Doi left blank.
